title: Sublinear-in-q prophet inequalities for q-matroid intersection
formal: Is there a function \(g:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to[1,\infty)\) with \(\lim_{q\to\infty}g(q)/q=0\) such that, for every sequence of independent nonnegative random values and every feasibility constraint given by the intersection of \(q\) matroids, some online irrevocable selection strategy obtains expected reward at least \(1/g(q)\) times the expected offline optimum? The arrival order is fixed in advance, all value distributions and constraints are known to the strategy, and the guarantee is independent of the number of elements.

source_formulation.text: Are there asymptotically better algorithms for the matroid intersection prophet inequality?
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 17

why: A prophet knows all random values before choosing a feasible set, while an online selector must commit before later values arrive. Matroid intersections capture many simultaneous resource constraints. Determining whether the approximation loss can grow sublinearly in their number would distinguish a limitation imposed by lack of future information from the performance of existing selection guarantees.
status_note: The 2023 source leaves the general asymptotic improvement open, and the author’s June 2024 note retains a corresponding restricted stochastic-matching question. The checked lower bound is sublinear and does not refute the target. Bounded subsequent-result searches through 2026-09-15 found no general resolution; this is not an exhaustive guarantee of current openness.

progress.text: As checked against the 2023 source’s explicit correction, Kleinberg and Weinberg provide a linear-in-\(q\) upper guarantee and a square-root lower-bound construction; their originally claimed matching linear lower bound was erroneous.
Saxena, Velusamy and Weinberg improve the lower bound to \(q^{1/2+\Omega(1/\log\log q)}\), retain the linear upper bounds, and ask in Section 6 for asymptotically better algorithms.
Velusamy’s stochastic-matching note poses asymptotically beating the linear approximation in the Bernoulli hypergraph-matching special case as Question 2.

category_assignment.reason: Sequential acceptance or selection must cope with unrevealed future values; prophet and secretary models belong to online algorithms.

importance.reason: This asks whether intersecting many independent feasibility constraints forces an essentially linear loss from sequential decisions even with full distributional knowledge and unlimited computation. Closing the gap would clarify a basic limitation of prophet inequalities and their use in stochastic allocation and mechanism design.
importance.basis: Individual review of the ITCS 2023 model, bounds and main open question, together with the author’s June 2024 stochastic-matching problem note.

sentences: Independent random element values arrive one at a time in a fixed known order.
The selector must irrevocably choose a set that is independent in each of q given matroids.
It knows the value distributions, while the offline comparator sees all realized values before making its choice.
The question asks whether the ratio of their expected rewards can always be bounded by a function growing sublinearly in q.
The checked source improves a square-root lower obstruction but corrects an earlier erroneous linear lower-bound claim and leaves the gap open.

definitions: Fix integers \(q,n\ge1\). The ground set is \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with elements arriving in the known order \(1,\ldots,n\). For each \(j\in[q]\), a matroid independence family \(\mathcal I_j\subseteq2^{[n]}\) contains \(\varnothing\), is hereditary, and satisfies augmentation: whenever \(A,B\in\mathcal I_j\) and \(|A|<|B|\), some \(b\in B\setminus A\) has \(A\cup\{b\}\in\mathcal I_j\). The feasible sets are \(\mathcal I=\bigcap_{j=1}^q\mathcal I_j\); repetitions among the matroids are allowed. For each \(t\), let \(D_t\) be an arbitrary Borel probability distribution on \([0,\infty)\) with finite first moment, and draw \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) independently with laws \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\). The offline optimum is \(\operatorname{OPT}(X)=\max_{S\in\mathcal I}\sum_{t\in S}X_t\), after all values have been revealed. An online strategy knows \(q,n,\mathcal I_1,\ldots,\mathcal I_q,D_1,\ldots,D_n\) in advance. Upon seeing \(X_t\), it accepts or rejects element \(t\) irrevocably. Its decision is a measurable function of \(t\), the observed prefix \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\), previous decisions and an internal random seed \(U\) uniform on \([0,1]\) and independent of all \(X_t\). Deterministic strategies may ignore \(U\). Every accepted prefix must be feasible, for every value sequence and seed, and previously accepted elements cannot be removed. Let \(S_{\mathcal A}(X,U)\) be the final accepted set and \(\operatorname{ALG}_{\mathcal A}(X,U)=\sum_{t\in S_{\mathcal A}(X,U)}X_t\). No bound on computation, distribution access or preprocessing is imposed; this is the information-theoretic online model. Exact distributions are part of the mathematical instance, not an implicit finite encoding or a sampling oracle. The target quantifiers are \(\exists g\;\forall q\ge1\;\forall n\ge1\;\forall(\mathcal I_j)_{j=1}^q\;\forall(D_t)_{t=1}^n\;\exists\mathcal A\) such that \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{ALG}_{\mathcal A}]\ge\mathbb E[\operatorname{OPT}]/g(q)\). Expectations include both the independent values and the independent internal seed. The first-moment assumption makes both expectations finite. The inequality also applies when the offline expectation is zero. The limit requirement means that for every \(\eta>0\), some \(q_0\) satisfies \(g(q)\le\eta q\) for all \(q\ge q_0\). The fixed arrival order represents any adversarially chosen order known before the random values are drawn; the order cannot adapt to their realizations.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the existence statement for one function \(g=o(q)\), including a policy with the stated guarantee for every instance, or a complete Lean-checked proof of the logical negation over all permitted strategies. Improving the constant in a linear \(Cq\) guarantee is insufficient. An \(o(q)\) result only for partition matroids, identical distributions, random arrival order or a bounded number of elements does not prove the full positive statement. A super-square-root lower bound that is itself \(o(q)\) does not refute it. There is no additional polynomial-time requirement.

context_blocks.text: The 2023 source asks whether asymptotically better matroid-intersection prophet inequalities exist. This card selects the \(o(q)\) improvement asked by the imported title, using the source’s unrestricted online-strategy benchmark rather than adding a polynomial-time computation requirement.

The source’s Theorem 7 records a general upper bound \(e(q+1)\) on the ratio of expected offline reward to expected online reward, where \(e\) is the base of the natural logarithm. The ratio compares two expectations, not an expectation of a ratio or a pointwise competitive guarantee.

The paper proves a lower bound \(q^{1/2+\Omega(1/\log\log q)}\), already for intersections of partition matroids with identical Bernoulli values. This improves a square-root obstruction while leaving room between the proved lower bound and linear upper bounds.

Footnote 3 explicitly corrects an earlier claimed \(\Omega(q)\) lower bound in Kleinberg and Weinberg’s work: that construction yields an \(\Omega(\sqrt q)\) obstruction. The correction does not invalidate their linear upper bound. Thus the earlier linear lower-bound claim cannot be used as a resolution of this question.

Velusamy’s June 2024 open-problem note again asks for an asymptotic improvement in online stochastic hypergraph matching with Bernoulli values, a partition-matroid subcase. That note supports the persistence of a restricted version and does not claim a general-matroid solution.
